title: Alert Concierge & Rollback Scenario Orchestrator for Ops
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: On-call engineers get PagerDuty/Slack alerts with shallow context (error message + service), which increases mean time to acknowledge and remediation. We want an "alert concierge" that enriches alerts with compact, actionable context and surfaces rollback candidates and a seeded postmortem/runbook draft to reduce cognitive load during incidents.

Goals:
- Attach a contextual bundle to PD incidents and Slack alert cards: short trace snippet (top 3 spans), recent log tail (last 20 lines filtered), metric slice (latency/error sparkline), and related deploy/commit metadata.
- Provide two actionable buttons: "Open Runbook" (pre-seeded checklist + remediation commands) and "Suggest Rollback" (lists probable rollback commits with risk score).
- Auto-seed a postmortem skeleton in Confluence on critical incidents after acknowledgment with templated prompts and links to evidence.

Non-goals:
- Not a full runbook authoring tool (Design provides link to existing runbook editor).
- No automatic rollback execution in this phase (user confirmation required).

Design/Architecture (summary):
- New service: alert-concierge-broker (stateless) subscribes to observability event stream (kafka) and to PagerDuty/Slack webhook events.
- When alert fires, broker resolves context: queries tracing API for top spans (bounded by size), fetches recent logs from log pipeline (with redact rules), computes metric deltas via our timeseries service, and queries deploy metadata store for candidate rollbacks (based on recent deploys and error correlation).
- To avoid sending large payloads directly to PD/Slack, concierge stores ephemeral artifacts (signed urls, TTL 1 hour) in internal artifacts storage and attaches compact references + a 300-char summary to the alert.
- Postmortem seeding: when incident severity >= P0 and acknowledged, broker invokes Confluence template API to create a postmortem draft with links to the artifact bundle and automated hypothesis scaffolding (failed checks, SLI deviation, suspect commit).

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We will prioritize small payloads for PD attachments (string summary + short signed ref). Full trace views open in internal UI to avoid PD size/security issues.
- Rollback candidate scoring: heuristic combining recent error spike correlation with deploy times, % of requests hitting a new revision, and dark-launch flags. We considered ML ranking but deferred to phase 2 due to training data scarcity.
- Security: redact PII from logs at collection time; signed artifact tokens must be short-lived (1h) and validated by auth proxy. This increases complexity vs embedding everything but meets compliance constraints.

Success criteria / acceptance criteria:
- When a PD incident is created for services A/B/C, the PD incident contains a concise context card with: top 3 spans, a 20-line log tail, a metric sparkline, and at least one rollback candidate.
- On severity P0 incidents, a Confluence postmortem draft is auto-created within 10 minutes of acknowledgment.
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTA) decreases by >= 15% on pilot services during the 2-week trial.
- No sensitive fields are leaked in attached artifact bundles (verified by automated redaction tests).

Monitoring / telemetry:
- New metrics: concierge.alerts_enriched, concierge.artifact_store_latencies, concierge.rollback_suggestions_count, postmortem.seed_success_rate.
- Dashboards: console-2026.03 will include an "Alert Concierge Health" dashboard with error rates, median enrichment latency, and token generation failures.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal canary: enable for infra-team alerts only (2 days).
2) Pilot: enable for three low-risk services (A/B/C) for 2 weeks and track MTA.
3) Gradual opt-in via Console toggles by team with audit logs for artifacts access.

Risks and mitigations:
- Artifact storage quotas: pre-allocated small TTL and gzip text; infra to increase quota if needed. (Raised ENG-23891)
- False rollback suggestions: limit to 3 candidates and show confidence score + link to changelist; require manual approval to execute.
- Token misuse: audit logs and short TTL + scope-limited tokens.

Open questions:
- Should the concierge attempt initial hypothesis prioritization (e.g., infra vs code) or leave that to the oncall? (Design prefers hypothesis hints; engineering prefers minimal scope.)
- Exact retention window for artifact signed URLs (1h vs 24h). Security prefers 1h.
acceptance_criteria:
- PD/Slack alerts enriched with compact context bundle (top spans, log tail, metric sparkline) for pilot services.
- Confluence postmortem draft auto-created for severity P0 incidents within 10 minutes of acknowledgment.
- Integration tests for redaction and token access pass in CI.
- Pilot shows >=15% reduction in MTA for pilot services.
